title: Three things that looked like resolutions this week all deferred the real question to later
explanation: A ceasefire, a court ruling, and a shipping framework all landed this week wearing the shape of a resolution — and in each case, the people closest to it said out loud that the actual question is still open. A peace roadmap got its first verification mission, not a verified peace. A Supreme Court stay resolved a procedural fight while its own justices noted the underlying legality is untouched. A transit deal is 'in principle' and 'still being finalized.' Each is a real step. None of them is the thing a headline would make it sound like.

evidence.text: Russia lifted its quarantine Oct 8, with the governor saying nearly 5,000 tests found no dangerous microorganisms and declaring the matter resolved - but the one question the quarantine was actually about, whether the lab worker died of plague, is exactly as unconfirmed as it was on day one.

The Nobel committee's pick was meant to honor institution-building, not settle anything - but Trump read it as a personal verdict, calling it 'disgraceful' and sanctioning the ICC within hours. Pillay escalated right back, calling the sanctions 'illegal' and predicting Netanyahu will stand trial - an honor that resolved nothing and opened a three-way fight instead.

Santa Cruz's civic leaders insist their demands don't include President Paz's resignation - just fuel imports and tax cuts. But their own Oct 10 deadline passed with no government response, and Evo Morales called his own supporters to protest starting today - a 'narrow' dispute now splitting into two fronts.

France's PM answered a month of school blockades with a letter deferring real decisions to 'fin octobre.' Each march since has only grown: Oct 17's broadened 'convergence des luttes' drew 800,000 (organizers) to 550,000 (Interior Ministry) - the dispute escalating rather than resolving.

retired.reason: Two of its four evidence items (Public Health/plague, Economic Policy/bolivia) are now 14-15 days old, well past the 10-day threshold, fed by storylines archived at the Oct 18 weekly rollover with no prospect of a fresh development. The recognition's own title frames these as events of 'this week,' which is no longer accurate for Oct 7-8 material three weeks later. The two live items (International Relations/Pillay, Education Policy/France) aren't enough on their own to meet the 3-4 item minimum, and no third fresh cross-domain item has emerged despite repeated searches across several cycles. Retiring now rather than continuing to carry two dead items under a 'this week' framing.
